- Compounds with only one halogen atom (Option B) may not be as effective in flame retardation because the effectiveness is often due to multiple halogen atoms.
- High molecular weight compounds with several halogens (Option C) are also used as fire retardants due to the presence of multiple halogen atoms which enhance flame retardation.
- Low molecular weight gases (Option D) are unlikely to be used as fire retardants due to their gaseous state and lower stability in terms of providing a retardant effect.
